claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately conveys the prohibition in § 91.107(a)(1) that no pilot may take off a civil aircraft unless the PIC ensures all passengers are briefed on seat belts and shoulder harnesses, subject to the lead-in conditions and aircraft exceptions.

Claim C0001 correctly represents the prohibition under § 91.107(a)(2) regarding surface movement, takeoff, or landing without ensuring passengers are notified to fasten safety belts and shoulder harnesses, retaining governing lead-in scope and exceptions.

Claim C0002 accurately sets forth the general requirement under § 91.107(a)(3) for each person on board to occupy an approved seat/berth with safety belts properly secured during surface movement, takeoff, and landing.
Claim C0003 captures the dock push-off and mooring personnel seating/belt exemption for seaplane and float-equipped rotorcraft operations during movement on the surface under § 91.107(a)(3).

Claim C0004 accurately reflects the lap-child permission under § 91.107(a)(3)(i), including the child age threshold (under 2 years old), adult seat requirement, absence of restraining device, and exception in § 91.108(j).
Claim C0005 accurately represents the sport parachuting floor-seating permission under § 91.107(a)(3)(ii).
Claim C0006 reflects the overarching permission for a child to occupy an approved child restraint system and the condition of accompaniment by an adult under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii).
Claim C0007 accurately conveys the labeling requirement under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(1) for child seats manufactured between January 1, 1981, and February 25, 1985.
Claim C0008 correctly describes the two required labels under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(2) for seats manufactured on or after February 26, 1985.

Claim C0009 captures the alternative approval and labeling routes under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(3) for child seats not qualifying under (B)(1) or (B)(2), correctly grouping UN standards, TC/STC approval, and TSO C-100b/§ 21.8(d) approval.
Claim C0010 accurately reproduces the grandfathering permission under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(3)(iv) for the AmSafe CARES device approved under § 21.305(d) (2010 ed.).
Claim C0011 correctly represents the prohibition against booster-type, vest-, harness-, and lap-held child restraint systems in aircraft under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(B)(4).
Claim C0012 correctly states the operator duty under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(1) requiring the restraint system to be properly secured to an approved forward-facing seat or berth.
Claim C0013 correctly conveys the operator duty under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(2) that the child be secured in the restraint system and not exceed its specified weight limit.
Claim C0014 accurately states the operator requirement under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(3) that the restraint system bear the appropriate label(s).
Claim C0015 accurately states the general operational scope exemption for operations conducted under 14 CFR part 121, 125, or 135 pursuant to § 91.107(b).
Claim C0016 correctly captures the exemption in § 91.107(b) stating that paragraph (a)(3) does not apply to persons subject to § 91.105.

unit_judgments.rationale: The prohibition on takeoff without passenger safety belt briefing is fully covered by claim C0000.
The prohibition on taxi/takeoff/landing without passenger notification to fasten safety belts is fully covered by claim C0001.
The requirement for passengers to occupy an approved seat/berth with safety belts secured during movement on the surface, takeoff, and landing is fully covered by claim C0002.
The dock push-off and mooring personnel seating exemption for seaplane and float-equipped rotorcraft operations is fully covered by claim C0003.
The permission for a child under age two to be held by an adult occupying an approved seat is fully covered by claim C0004.
The permission for sport parachutists to use the floor of the aircraft as a seat is fully covered by claim C0005.
The permission to occupy an approved child restraint system when accompanied by a parent, guardian, or attendant is fully covered by claim C0006.
The labeling requirement for child restraint seats manufactured between Jan 1, 1981, and Feb 25, 1985, is fully covered by claim C0007.
The two-label requirement for child restraint seats manufactured on or after Feb 26, 1985, is fully covered by claim C0008.
The alternative approval label showing manufacture under United Nations standards is covered by the grouped alternative claim C0009.
The alternative approval label showing FAA Type Certificate or Supplemental Type Certificate approval is covered by the grouped alternative claim C0009.
The alternative approval label showing FAA approval under § 21.8(d) or TSO C-100b is covered by the grouped alternative claim C0009.
The labeling continuation permission for the AmSafe CARES device approved under § 21.305(d) is fully covered by claim C0010.
The prohibition on booster-type, vest-, harness-, and lap-held child restraints is fully covered by claim C0011.
The operator duty to secure the restraint system to an approved forward-facing seat or berth is fully covered by claim C0012.
The operator duty to ensure the child is properly secured and does not exceed the restraint's weight limit is fully covered by claim C0013.
The operator duty to ensure the child restraint bears appropriate label(s) is fully covered by claim C0014.
The exemption of part 121, 125, and 135 operations from § 91.107 is fully covered by claim C0015.
The exemption of persons subject to § 91.105 from § 91.107(a)(3) is fully covered by claim C0016.
